problem.text: The special-token encoding path split text around literal token spellings and inserted mapped IDs itself, withholding those tokens and their surrounding context from the backend tokenizer.

reasoning.text: Passing the complete input to the backend delegates token recognition and whitespace handling to that engine rather than duplicating recognition with a regular expression. The retained TODO explicitly leaves the necessity of the old SentencePiece-oriented workaround unresolved.

impact.text: encode_special now returns one backend encoding with add_special_tokens=False. Explicit BOS/EOS insertion and batch padding remain in encode; the change does not alter decoding.

source_notes.text: The earlier loading-tokenization entry identifies the manual path's lack of AddedToken whitespace rules and reports Phi configurations with rstrip=true. That is historical explanatory context, not a fresh inspection of those model artifacts.

The whole-parent Phi search found a Phi3/Phi4 prompt formatter alongside incidental calibration-text matches. The formatter places newlines after role and end markers, making token-adjacent whitespace locally relevant without establishing a reproduced Phi failure.

limitations: No Hugging Face tokenizer, model-specific tokenization, or generation test was executed. Actual lstrip/rstrip behavior and compatibility across tokenizer files remain unverified.
The standard-library check models regex segmentation and decoding filters only; it does not execute the repository tokenizer.
The broad Phi search was truncated by calibration-text matches and does not establish an exhaustive inventory of related source.

chapters.title: Delegate special-token encoding to the backend

claims.text: Previously, encode_special lazily compiled escaped extended-vocabulary spellings into a capturing regex, encoded the intervening fragments separately, and inserted special IDs directly. The patch comments out that implementation and encodes the entire text once instead.

The backend is loaded from tokenizer.json. Separate added_tokens.json and special added_tokens_decoder entries still populate wrapper lookup dictionaries, but the new encode_special no longer consults those dictionaries. Correct special-token recognition therefore depends on the backend's loaded definitions rather than wrapper-side ID substitution.

The direct caller is encode_special_or_unspecial when special is true; encode reaches it for both scalar and batched input through encode_special_tokens. The ordinary branch is unchanged and already delegates directly when its unspecial mapping is empty.

A scalar transcription using '<|user|>
hello<|end|>
' produced ordinary fragments '
hello' and '
' under the old split. This demonstrates that the old wrapper sent those newlines separately from the special tokens; it does not establish what the backend emits for the replacement whole-text call.

The tradeoff is removal of manual token-boundary enforcement in favor of backend semantics. This gives the backend complete context but does not prove equivalence for tokens represented only in the wrapper's auxiliary mappings.

Inspection against the task diff shows that inherited decoding limitations remain: EOS filtering precedes attempted truncation, extended IDs outside backend vocabulary are filtered, and rank-two decoding returns a list even for one row. The padding fallback, ordinal-table construction, and ordinary encoding branch also remain unchanged; this patch is not a general tokenizer compatibility repair.

findings.description: Unchanged decode_ filtering prevents its EOS truncation branch from working and discards extended IDs outside backend vocabulary before special rendering.
findings.trigger: Decode a sequence containing EOS followed by ordinary tokens, or request special rendering of a mapped ID at or beyond backend vocabulary size.
findings.expected_behavior: The explicit EOS truncation branch should discard the suffix; special rendering should retain a mapped extended token.
findings.actual_behavior: EOS is removed before truncation can find it, while the vocabulary-bound filter removes extended IDs before dictionary rendering.

verification.description: Whole-parent search finds direct calls from both rank-one and rank-two branches of decode. Both pass through the inspected filters, which the task leaves unchanged.
verification.limits: Broader generation workflows were not traced; no backend decoding ran.

verification.description: With EOS=2, PAD=0 and vocabulary size 50, the filter transformed [11,2,12,0,99] into [11,12], retaining the token after EOS.
verification.limits: Python list filtering only, not repository execution.

findings.description: decode retains its mismatch between the documented one-sequence return type and rank-two handling.
findings.trigger: Pass a rank-two tensor with one row to Tokenizer.decode.
findings.expected_behavior: Its docstring promises a string when batch size is one.
findings.actual_behavior: The rank-two branch returns a one-element list. The internal recursive call for list inputs also uses this rank-dependent behavior.

verification.description: Compared the docstring and rank-two return branch with the task's encode_special-only edit.
verification.limits: No tensor execution or inventory of external decode callers was performed; reach is limited here to the public method's stated input contract.

annotation.summary: Replaces manual special-token splitting with whole-text backend encoding, enabling backend-controlled token handling while leaving compatibility and inherited decoding limitations unresolved.

argv:
import re,json
text='<|user|>\nhello<|end|>\n'
pieces={'<|user|>':32010,'<|end|>':32007}
split=re.compile('('+'|'.join(map(re.escape,pieces))+')').split(text)
seq=[11,2,12,0,99]; eos=2; pad=0; vocab=50
filtered=[t for t in seq if t != pad and t < vocab and t != eos]
if eos in filtered: filtered=filtered[:filtered.index(eos)]
print(json.dumps({'old_split':split,'ordinary_segments':[split[i] for i in range(0,len(split),2) if split[i]],'decode_filtered':filtered}))
